title: How to Measure Your Kitchen for RTA Cabinets
metaTitle: How to Measure Your Kitchen for Cabinets
description: A step by step guide to measuring your kitchen walls, corners, and openings so your White Shaker RTA cabinet order fits right the first time.
intro: Accurate measurements are the foundation of a smooth cabinet order. Before you build a list in our free 3D Kitchen Planner or request a quote, spend twenty minutes with a tape measure and this checklist so your White Shaker cabinets arrive ready to fit.

sections.heading: What you need before you start
sections.body:
Grab a steel tape measure at least 25 feet long, a notepad or your phone, a pencil, and a helper if you can find one. A laser measure is handy but not required. Sketch a rough top down outline of your kitchen first, marking every wall, window, door, and appliance location. You will fill in exact numbers as you go.

Measure in inches to the nearest eighth inch. Cabinet manufacturers work in fractions of an inch, and rounding to the nearest inch is the most common cause of a tight or gappy fit.

sections.heading: Measure each wall in three places
sections.body:
Walls are rarely perfectly straight or square. For every wall that will hold cabinets, measure the total length at the top, the middle, and the bottom (near the floor). Use the smallest of the three numbers as your working length, since that is the tightest constraint your cabinet run has to fit inside.

Also measure wall height from the floor to the ceiling in at least two spots, and check the floor for slope with a level. Older homes in particular can be out of level by half an inch or more across a run, which affects how you plan base cabinets and toe kicks.

sections.heading: Note windows, doors, and obstructions
sections.body:
For every window and door on a cabinet wall, record:
- Distance from the nearest corner to the edge of the trim
- Width of the window or door opening including trim
- Height from the floor to the bottom of the window sill

Also mark the location of outlets, switches, plumbing stub outs, gas lines, and any vents or radiators. These details matter when you are placing sinks, ranges, and upper cabinets in the planner, since RTA boxes cannot be trimmed around obstructions the way custom cabinetry can.

sections.heading: Check your corners
sections.body:
Measure into each corner from both directions, and confirm whether the corner is a true 90 degrees using a large square or by measuring a triangle (a three four five foot check works well). Out of square corners are common and usually just mean a filler strip is needed next to the first cabinet in the run, which is normal and easy to plan for.

Decide early whether each corner will be a blind corner cabinet, a lazy Susan style corner, or an open run that simply stops short of the corner. This decision affects the length available for the rest of your cabinets.

sections.heading: Standard clearances to plan around
sections.body:
- Leave at least 42 inches of clear walkway in a single cook kitchen, and 48 inches where two people work at once
- Plan 36 inches of counter space next to a sink and 15 inches next to a range where possible
- Standard base cabinets are 34.5 inches tall and 24 inches deep, with wall cabinets typically mounted 18 inches above the counter
- Wall cabinets are 12 inches deep and currently ship in a 36 inch tall standard line, with a 30 inch tall line coming soon for kitchens with lower ceilings

sections.heading: Bring it all together
sections.body: Once you have every wall, corner, window, door, and obstruction measured, transfer your sketch into the free 3D Kitchen Planner at /planner. The planner lets you drag and drop cabinets to your exact wall lengths so you can see fit issues before you order rather than after a box arrives. If anything looks tight or you are unsure about a corner or an appliance opening, include a note when you request your quote and our team will double check it with you before confirming your order.

faqs.q: What if my walls are not perfectly straight?
faqs.a: Almost no wall is perfectly straight. Use the smallest measurement of the three you take, and plan for a filler panel to absorb small variations. This is standard practice and keeps your cabinet doors and drawers aligned.

faqs.q: Do I need to hire a professional to measure my kitchen?
faqs.a: Most homeowners can measure accurately using this guide and a tape measure. If your kitchen has unusual angles, a large island, or several structural obstructions, you are welcome to send us photos and measurements and we will help review your plan before you order.

faqs.q: How accurate do my measurements need to be?
faqs.a: Aim for accuracy within an eighth of an inch on wall lengths and corner distances. Small variations are normal and handled with fillers, but errors of an inch or more can cause real fit problems.

title: How to Assemble Your RTA Cabinets
description: Step by step instructions for assembling flat packed White Shaker RTA cabinets at home, from unboxing to hanging doors and installing drawer glides.
intro: Our White Shaker RTA cabinets ship flat packed with all assembly hardware included, using a simple cam lock and dowel system designed for home assembly. Most cabinets can be built in 20 to 40 minutes once you get the hang of the process. Here is how to do it right.

sections.heading: Tools you will need
sections.body:
- Phillips screwdriver or a drill with a Phillips bit
- Rubber mallet
- Level
- Clean, flat work surface such as a table or the floor covered with a moving blanket
- The hardware bag included in each cabinet box, plus the included cam locks, dowels, and screws

sections.heading: Step 1: Unpack and check parts
sections.body:
Open each cabinet box carefully and lay out all panels, the hardware bag, doors, and drawer fronts. Compare what you have against the parts list included in the box. If anything is missing or damaged, contact us at service@rtacabinetscanada.ca before you begin assembly so we can send a replacement quickly.

Work on one cabinet at a time and keep hardware bags separated by cabinet so you do not mix up parts between boxes.

sections.heading: Step 2: Attach the sides to the top and bottom
sections.body:
Most cabinet boxes use cam locks paired with dowels for a tool light, tight fitting joint. Insert the dowels into the pre drilled holes on the bottom and top panels, then align the side panels and press together by hand. Insert the cam bolts into the side panels and turn each cam lock a quarter turn with a screwdriver until it clicks and draws the joint tight.

Work through all four corners before fully tightening any one of them, then go back and snug each cam lock evenly. This keeps the box square instead of pulling it out of alignment.

sections.heading: Step 3: Attach the back panel
sections.body: Slide the back panel into the grooves or rabbets along the top, bottom, and side panels as shown in your instructions, then secure it with the small screws provided. The back panel squares up the entire box, so check with a level or by measuring both diagonals of the cabinet, they should match, before moving on.

sections.heading: Step 4: Install shelves and hang doors
sections.body:
Insert shelf pins at your desired height and set the adjustable shelves in place. To hang doors, attach the hinge cups to the pre drilled holes on the inside of the door, then screw the hinge plates to the cabinet side panel. Snap the door onto the hinge plate and use the adjustment screws on the hinge to fine tune the gap so doors sit even and flush.

Our soft close hinges and drawer glides are self damping, so doors and drawers will ease shut on their own once installed correctly. No extra adjustment is needed for the soft close action itself.

sections.heading: Step 5: Install drawers and glides
sections.body: Mount the drawer glide rails to the inside of the cabinet at the marked height, making sure both sides are level with each other. Attach the matching glide hardware to the drawer box, then slide the drawer onto the rails until it clicks into place. Test the drawer to confirm it slides smoothly and closes evenly before loading it.

sections.heading: A few tips for a cleaner build
sections.body:
- Do not fully tighten cam locks until all four corners are engaged
- Keep a rubber mallet handy for gently seating dowels, never use a metal hammer directly on the panels
- Assemble in a clean, dust free area to avoid scratching the painted white finish
- If a joint feels tight, check that the dowel is fully seated rather than forcing the cam lock

If you would rather skip assembly altogether, our expert assembly service builds every cabinet before it is delivered for 75 dollars per cabinet.

faqs.q: How long does it take to assemble one cabinet?
faqs.a: Most base and wall cabinets take 20 to 40 minutes for a first time builder, and less once you get comfortable with the cam lock system. A full kitchen is usually a weekend project for two people.

faqs.q: Do I need special tools?
faqs.a: No. A Phillips screwdriver or drill, a rubber mallet, and a level are enough for every cabinet in your order. All hardware is included in the box.

faqs.q: What if a part is missing or damaged?
faqs.a: Email service@rtacabinetscanada.ca with your order number and a photo of the issue and we will send a replacement part promptly.

faqs.q: Can I have someone assemble the cabinets for me?
faqs.a: Yes. Our expert assembly service builds every cabinet in your order before it is delivered, for 75 dollars per cabinet.

title: How to Install Your Kitchen Cabinets
description: A practical, step by step guide to installing base and wall cabinets, from finding studs and setting a level line to hanging uppers and fitting fillers.
intro: Once your White Shaker cabinets are assembled, installing them correctly is what makes the finished kitchen look and function like a professional job. This guide walks through the order of operations most installers follow, from marking your level line through the final toe kick.

sections.heading: Before you start
sections.body: Confirm your walls are marked for stud locations using a stud finder, and mark each stud with a vertical pencil line that extends above where your wall cabinets will sit. Shut off any electrical circuits you will be working near, and remove baseboards along the cabinet run if you plan to run cabinets to the finished floor.

sections.heading: Step 1: Establish your level line
sections.body:
Find the highest point of your floor along the cabinet run using a level, since base cabinets are set level from that point and shimmed up everywhere else. Measure up 34.5 inches from that high point (the standard base cabinet height) and snap a level chalk line around the room. This line represents the top of your base cabinets and is the single most important reference in the whole install.

Measure up from the base cabinet line to mark where the bottom of your wall cabinets will sit, typically 18 inches above where the counter surface will land.

sections.heading: Step 2: Install a ledger board
sections.body: Temporarily screw a straight board along the wall cabinet line to support the weight of the upper cabinets while you fasten them. This lets you position and level each cabinet without holding it in place by hand, and makes the install dramatically easier for one or two people.

sections.heading: Step 3: Hang the wall cabinets first
sections.body:
Installing upper cabinets before base cabinets gives you room to work without leaning over counters. Start in a corner, rest the cabinet on the ledger board, and check it for level and plumb in both directions. Drive screws through the cabinet back rail into wall studs, using at least two screws per stud location.

Clamp or screw adjoining wall cabinets together through their face frames before fully tightening the wall screws, so the fronts stay flush and the door gaps stay even across the whole run. Work down the wall one cabinet at a time, checking level at each step since small errors compound quickly.

sections.heading: Step 4: Set the base cabinets
sections.body:
Starting again from a corner, set the first base cabinet on your level line and shim underneath as needed to bring it level front to back and side to side. Screw through the back rail into wall studs where possible. Attach the next cabinet by clamping the face frames flush and driving cabinet screws through the adjoining frames, then screw it to the wall and check level again before moving to the next cabinet.

Use a level across the tops of several cabinets at once as you go to make sure the whole run stays consistent, not just each cabinet individually.

sections.heading: Step 5: Fillers, corners, and panels
sections.body: Filler strips close small gaps at walls and corners and are trimmed to width with a table saw or circular saw before being screwed to the adjoining cabinet. Fit fillers snugly against the wall, especially in corners where walls are rarely perfectly square. Finish panels dress up any exposed cabinet sides and are attached the same way as fillers, with screws from the inside of the adjacent cabinet.

sections.heading: Step 6: Toe kicks and final checks
sections.body:
Once all base cabinets are set, level, and secured, attach the toe kick along the bottom front of the run, scribing it to the floor if the floor is uneven. Remove the wall cabinet ledger board and touch up screw holes. Do a final walk through checking that every door and drawer opens, closes, and aligns evenly, and adjust hinges as needed.

If you would rather not tackle installation yourself, our expert assembly service builds cabinets before delivery, which simplifies the install to setting and securing finished boxes.

faqs.q: Should I install wall cabinets or base cabinets first?
faqs.a: Wall cabinets first, using a temporary ledger board to hold them at height. This gives you clear access to the wall without base cabinets in the way, and is the order most professional installers use.

faqs.q: What if my walls or floor are not level?
faqs.a: This is common and expected. Base cabinets are leveled from the highest point of the floor using shims underneath, and wall cabinets are leveled independently against a chalk line, not against an uneven floor or ceiling.

faqs.q: Do I need to screw into studs?
faqs.a: Yes. Cabinets should always be fastened into wall studs wherever possible, with at least two screws per stud for wall cabinets given the weight they carry once loaded.

title: RTA vs Custom vs Big Box Store Cabinets
metaTitle: RTA vs Custom vs Big Box Cabinets
description: Comparing ready to assemble, custom, and big box store cabinets on cost, materials, lead time, and quality to help you choose the right option for your kitchen.
intro: Homeowners renovating a kitchen usually choose between three paths: ready to assemble (RTA) cabinets, fully custom cabinetry, and pre assembled cabinets from a big box home improvement store. Each has real tradeoffs in cost, materials, and timeline.

sections.heading: Ready to assemble (RTA) cabinets
sections.body:
RTA cabinets ship flat packed and are assembled at home using included hardware, which removes most of the labour and shipping cost built into other options. Our White Shaker RTA line uses plywood boxes with solid hardwood face frames and doors, painted white, with soft close doors and drawers included as standard.

Because the cost structure skips factory assembly and reduces shipping volume, RTA cabinets typically deliver solid wood and plywood construction at a price point closer to laminate big box cabinets, without giving up material quality. The tradeoff is that assembly and installation are on you, or handled through an optional assembly service.

sections.heading: Custom cabinetry
sections.body:
Custom cabinets are built to order by a local cabinet shop or factory, with full control over dimensions, finishes, and configurations. This is the most flexible option and the best fit for unusual layouts or specific design visions, but it comes with the highest price point and the longest lead times, often eight to sixteen weeks or more depending on the shop's backlog.

Custom is worth the investment when your kitchen has non standard dimensions throughout, or when you want finishes and configurations that off the shelf lines simply do not offer.

sections.heading: Big box store cabinets
sections.body:
Big box home improvement stores sell both stock and semi custom cabinet lines, usually pre assembled or assembled in store for a fee. Selection is convenient and lead times can be short for in stock items, but materials often lean toward particleboard boxes and thinner veneers at the lower price tiers, with solid wood construction reserved for higher priced lines.

Big box cabinets are a reasonable choice for a fast, budget renovation where long term durability is a lower priority than getting a kitchen finished quickly.

sections.heading: How they compare
sections.body:
- Cost: RTA is typically the best value for solid wood construction, custom is the most expensive, big box varies widely by line
- Materials: our RTA line uses plywood boxes with solid hardwood frames and doors, custom varies by shop, big box varies from particleboard to solid wood depending on price tier
- Lead time: RTA orders ship in 2 to 3 weeks, custom often runs 8 to 16 weeks, big box in stock items can be immediate but special orders take weeks
- Labour: RTA requires home assembly (or a paid assembly service), custom and many big box lines arrive pre assembled
- Selection: custom offers the most flexibility, RTA and big box offer curated but growing option sets

sections.heading: Which is right for you
sections.body: If your kitchen has fairly standard dimensions and you want solid wood construction without a custom price tag or a months long wait, RTA is usually the sweet spot. If you have unusual layout requirements or want a completely bespoke design, custom cabinetry is worth the extra cost and time. If speed and the lowest possible upfront cost matter most and you are comfortable with lighter duty materials, a big box option may fit your project.

sections.heading: A note on assembly and installation
sections.body: One tradeoff worth planning for with RTA is that assembly and installation require either your own time or a paid service. Custom and most big box cabinets typically arrive ready to install, which shifts labour cost into the purchase price rather than leaving it as a separate step. If you would rather skip assembly, our expert assembly service builds every cabinet before delivery for 75 dollars per cabinet, giving you the RTA price and material advantage without the do it yourself assembly step.

sections.heading: Total cost of ownership
sections.body: When comparing options, it helps to think beyond the sticker price alone. Solid wood construction, like the plywood boxes and hardwood face frames used in our White Shaker line, tends to hold up better over years of daily use than particleboard, which can mean fewer repairs or replacements down the road regardless of which category you choose it from. Factor in delivery costs as well, since free local delivery within 300 km of London, Ontario can meaningfully offset the price difference between options for many Southwestern Ontario homeowners.

faqs.q: Are RTA cabinets lower quality than custom cabinets?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Our White Shaker RTA cabinets use plywood boxes and solid hardwood face frames and doors, the same core materials used in many custom shops. The difference is standardized sizing and home assembly rather than a difference in material quality.

faqs.q: How much faster is RTA than custom cabinetry?
faqs.a: Our RTA orders ship in 2 to 3 weeks, while custom cabinetry commonly takes 8 to 16 weeks or longer depending on the shop. RTA is a strong option when your timeline is tight.

faqs.q: Can I mix RTA cabinets with a custom island or unique piece?
faqs.a: Many homeowners do exactly this, using RTA for the bulk of the kitchen and a custom shop for one statement piece. Talk to us about your layout when you request a quote and we can help you plan around it.

title: White Shaker Kitchen Design Ideas
description: Design inspiration for White Shaker kitchens, covering hardware finishes, countertop and backsplash pairings, islands, and wall cabinet height options.
intro: White Shaker cabinets are a design classic because they work with nearly any style, from farmhouse to modern to transitional. Here are practical ideas for finishing out a White Shaker kitchen you will love for years.

sections.heading: Choosing hardware
sections.body:
Hardware is the single easiest way to shift the personality of a White Shaker kitchen. Matte black pulls read modern and high contrast, brushed brass or gold lean warm and traditional, and brushed nickel or chrome sit quietly in between and pair well with stainless appliances. Bar pulls on drawers and doors give a clean, linear look, while cup pulls or knobs suit more traditional spaces.

As a general rule, use one finish consistently throughout the kitchen rather than mixing metals, and choose a pull length proportional to your door and drawer sizes, longer pulls on wider drawers, shorter pulls or knobs on doors.

sections.heading: Countertop pairings
sections.body: White Shaker cabinets pair well with almost any countertop material because the cabinet colour is neutral. Quartz in soft white or warm greige keeps things bright and low maintenance. Butcher block adds warmth and works especially well on an island for contrast against white perimeter cabinets. Darker stone or quartz countertops, such as charcoal or deep green, create striking contrast against the white boxes and are a popular choice for a bolder look.

sections.heading: Backsplash ideas
sections.body: Classic subway tile in white or a soft neutral keeps a White Shaker kitchen timeless. For more visual interest, a herringbone pattern, a colourful zellige tile, or a bold patterned tile behind the range as a focal point all work well against the simple lines of Shaker doors. Extending the backsplash to the ceiling behind open shelving or a range hood is a popular way to add height and drama without changing the cabinet colour.

sections.heading: Planning an island
sections.body: An island is a natural place to introduce contrast in a White Shaker kitchen. Consider a painted colour, a stained wood tone, or a mixed material base while keeping the perimeter cabinets white. Plan for at least 42 inches of clearance around the island for walkways, and 36 inches if seating is only on one side. Use the free 3D Kitchen Planner at /planner to test island sizes against your actual room dimensions before ordering.

sections.heading: Choosing your wall cabinet height
sections.body: Our White Shaker line ships with 36 inch tall wall cabinets as the standard option, which is a good match for kitchens with 8 to 9 foot ceilings and a desire to maximize storage all the way up. A 30 inch tall wall cabinet line is coming soon for kitchens with lower ceilings or a preference for open space above the cabinets, such as for display shelving or a decorative treatment. If your ceiling height is under 8 feet, mention it when you request your quote so we can help you plan the best fit.

sections.heading: Open shelving and mixed storage
sections.body: Many White Shaker kitchens mix a few open shelves with closed upper cabinets, especially flanking a range hood or above a sink where reaching into a closed cabinet is less convenient. Open shelving works best kept simple and uncluttered, styled with a handful of everyday dishes or a few plants rather than a fully packed display.

sections.heading: Wall colour and cabinet contrast
sections.body: White Shaker cabinets can either blend softly into a light, neutral wall colour for a bright, airy feel, or stand out against a deeper wall colour such as sage green, navy, or warm greige. If your kitchen is open to a living or dining area, consider how your wall colour choice will read from adjoining rooms, since White Shaker cabinets tend to visually recede against light walls and pop forward against darker ones.

sections.heading: Lighting considerations
sections.body: Under cabinet lighting is a popular addition beneath wall cabinets, both for task lighting at the counter and for highlighting a tile backsplash in the evening. Pendant lighting over an island pairs naturally with White Shaker cabinetry and gives you another place to introduce a metal finish that complements your hardware choice. Plan your electrical layout for under cabinet lighting before your wall cabinets go up, since running wire behind an installed cabinet is far more difficult than planning for it during installation.

faqs.q: What hardware finish looks best with White Shaker cabinets?
faqs.a: There is no single right answer since White Shaker is neutral enough to suit matte black, brushed brass, or brushed nickel equally well. Choose based on your appliance finishes and the overall style you are going for, and stay consistent throughout the kitchen.

faqs.q: Should I choose 36 inch or 30 inch wall cabinets?
faqs.a: 36 inch wall cabinets, our current standard, maximize storage and suit most 8 to 9 foot ceilings. Our 30 inch line, coming soon, suits lower ceilings or kitchens where you want open wall space above the cabinets.

faqs.q: Can I see how a design will look before ordering?
faqs.a: Yes. Build your layout in the free 3D Kitchen Planner at /planner to see your cabinet run, island, and overall kitchen shape before you request a quote.

title: Kitchen Cabinet Sizes Explained
description: A clear breakdown of standard cabinet widths, heights, and depths, plus how fillers and corner cabinets work, so you can plan your layout with confidence.
intro: Cabinet sizing follows a set of long standing industry standards that make planning a kitchen much easier once you understand them. Here is a plain explanation of the numbers you will see while building your list.

sections.heading: Standard cabinet heights and depths
sections.body:
- Base cabinets: 34.5 inches tall, 24 inches deep, designed to bring your finished counter to the common 36 inch counter height once a countertop is added
- Wall cabinets: 12 inches deep, currently available in a 36 inch tall standard line, with a 30 inch tall line coming soon
- Tall or pantry cabinets: typically span from the floor close to ceiling height and share the 24 inch depth of base cabinets

These dimensions are shared across most North American cabinet manufacturers, which is part of why RTA cabinets fit so predictably into existing kitchen layouts.

sections.heading: Standard cabinet widths
sections.body:
Cabinets are typically available in widths that increase in 3 inch increments, commonly starting around 9 inches for a slim base or wall cabinet and running up to 36 inches or wider for larger base and sink cabinets. Wider cabinets reduce the number of seams in a run, while narrower cabinets offer more flexibility to fit a specific wall length exactly.

When planning a run, add up your available wall length and work backward from standard widths, saving any leftover space for a filler rather than trying to force a non standard cabinet width.

sections.heading: Understanding fillers
sections.body: A filler is a plain panel, typically 3 inches wide, installed at the end of a cabinet run next to a wall, appliance, or corner. Fillers absorb the small measurement variations that are normal in any real kitchen, and they give doors and drawers room to open fully without hitting an adjacent wall or appliance handle. Every cabinet layout should include at least a small filler wherever a cabinet run meets a wall at an angle or a fixed obstruction.

sections.heading: Corner cabinet options
sections.body: Corners can be handled a few different ways. A blind corner base cabinet extends one cabinet partially into the corner with the adjoining cabinet covering the rest, giving usable if slightly harder to reach storage. A lazy Susan or corner carousel cabinet uses rotating shelves to make corner storage fully accessible. Diagonal corner cabinets present an angled door facing into the room and work well in open layouts. Your choice depends on your storage priorities and how much you want to spend on corner hardware.

sections.heading: Putting sizes together in your layout
sections.body: Once you know your wall lengths from measuring, choose cabinet widths that get as close as possible to filling the space, then plan a filler for the remainder. The free 3D Kitchen Planner at /planner shows running totals as you add cabinets so you can see exactly how much wall length is left as you build your list, which makes fitting standard sizes into a real kitchen straightforward even without cabinetry experience.

sections.heading: Sink and appliance cabinet sizing
sections.body: Sink base cabinets are typically wider than a standard base cabinet, commonly 30 to 36 inches, to accommodate the sink bowl and plumbing while leaving room on either side for the cabinet frame. Appliance cabinets, such as those built around a dishwasher, range, or built in oven, follow the appliance manufacturer's specified opening dimensions rather than a standard cabinet width, so always check your specific appliance's installation manual for the required width, height, and depth before finalizing that part of your layout.

sections.heading: Mixing wall cabinet heights in one kitchen
sections.body: It is common to use a shorter wall cabinet above a range hood, refrigerator, or window than the standard height used elsewhere in the kitchen, simply because the space available above those areas is smaller. Our 36 inch standard wall cabinets cover most of a kitchen's upper storage, while shorter runs above appliances or windows may call for a different height, which our team can help you plan for when you request your quote.

faqs.q: Why do cabinets come in 3 inch width increments?
faqs.a: It is a long standing industry standard that keeps manufacturing efficient and makes it easier to mix and match cabinets from different runs or even different suppliers into a coherent layout.

faqs.q: Do I always need a filler?
faqs.a: Not always, but most real kitchens need at least a small filler somewhere in the layout because wall lengths rarely divide evenly into standard cabinet widths. It is normal and expected, not a sign of a poor fit.

faqs.q: What is the standard counter height and how does that affect base cabinets?
faqs.a: Base cabinets are 34.5 inches tall, which brings the finished height to the common 36 inch counter height once a standard countertop thickness is added on top.

title: Shipping, Delivery, and Free Local Delivery
description: How RTA Cabinets Canada delivers your order, including our free 300 km local delivery area, Canada wide freight, and what to check when boxes arrive.
intro: Getting a full kitchen order from our warehouse to your door involves a few moving parts. Here is exactly how delivery works, what is included for free, and what to do when your cabinets arrive.

sections.heading: Free local delivery
sections.body: Any delivery address within 300 km of London, Ontario qualifies for free delivery. This covers a wide area of Southwestern Ontario, and we will confirm whether your address falls within the free zone when you request your quote. There is no minimum order size required to qualify.

sections.heading: Canada wide freight shipping
sections.body: For addresses beyond the 300 km free delivery zone, we quote Canada wide freight shipping based on your postal code. Freight costs depend on distance, order size, and destination accessibility, and the exact quote is provided along with your cabinet pricing so there are no surprises before you confirm your order.

sections.heading: Curbside delivery
sections.body: Deliveries, whether local or freight, are curbside. The carrier will bring your boxes to the delivery address at ground level, but moving boxes into the house, upstairs, or into a specific room is the responsibility of the customer or their contractor. Plan to have help available on delivery day, especially for larger kitchen orders with dozens of boxes.

sections.heading: Inspecting your delivery
sections.body:
As soon as your order arrives, count the boxes against your packing list and do a visual check of each box for crushed corners, punctures, or water damage before the carrier leaves if possible. Open boxes within a few days to confirm the contents match your order and that panels are not damaged.

Damage must be reported within 48 hours of delivery. Email service@rtacabinetscanada.ca with your order number, a description of the issue, and photos of both the damaged item and the box it arrived in, and we will arrange a replacement promptly.

sections.heading: Lead times
sections.body: In stock White Shaker cabinet orders typically ship within 2 to 3 weeks of a confirmed order. Many local deliveries within the free zone arrive sooner than that once the order is ready. Lead times can vary slightly based on order size and current volume, and we will confirm an expected timeframe when your quote is finalized.

sections.heading: Preparing for delivery day
sections.body:
Before your delivery arrives, clear a path from the driveway or curb to where you plan to stage the boxes, and confirm you have enough dry, flat indoor space to store a full kitchen's worth of flat packed cabinets until you are ready to assemble and install them. Arrange for extra hands on delivery day, since a full kitchen order can be dozens of individual boxes, some of them large and awkward for one person to carry alone.

If you know your delivery window will be tight for scheduling, such as needing someone home to receive the shipment, let us know when you confirm your order and we will do what we can to coordinate timing with the carrier.

sections.heading: Freight destinations outside our service area
sections.body: For freight shipments beyond the 300 km free zone, more remote destinations, rural routes, or locations without regular freight service may take a little longer or carry a higher freight cost than a major city on a standard route. We calculate freight based on your specific postal code so the quote you receive reflects your actual delivery address rather than a generic regional estimate.

sections.heading: Packaging and what to expect in each box
sections.body: Cabinets ship flat packed in sturdy, individually labelled boxes, with each box corresponding to one cabinet in your order. Doors, panels, and hardware are protected with foam corners and edge padding to reduce the chance of transit damage. Keep your packing list handy as boxes arrive so you can match each label to your order and confirm nothing is missing before you begin unpacking and sorting for assembly.

faqs.q: How do I know if I qualify for free delivery?
faqs.a: Any address within 300 km of London, Ontario qualifies. Provide your delivery address or postal code when you request a quote and we will confirm whether you are in the free zone or provide a freight quote.

faqs.q: What does curbside delivery mean?
faqs.a: The carrier delivers your boxes to your driveway or curb at ground level. Carrying boxes into the house or to a specific floor is not included, so plan to have help on hand for a full kitchen order.

faqs.q: What do I do if a box arrives damaged?
faqs.a: Check boxes for damage on arrival and report any issue to service@rtacabinetscanada.ca within 48 hours with photos and your order number so we can send a replacement quickly.

title: Financing and Our Lowest Price Guarantee
description: Learn how 0% APR financing works for your cabinet order and how our Lowest Price Guarantee matches verified pricing on identical in stock cabinets.
intro: A kitchen renovation is a meaningful investment, and we want paying for it to be as flexible and fair as possible. Here is how financing works and how our price match guarantee protects you.

sections.heading: 0% APR financing
sections.body:
We offer 0% APR financing on approved credit through a third party lender, letting you spread the cost of your cabinet order across monthly instalments instead of paying the full amount upfront. To use financing, you apply through the lender's application process once your quote is finalized, receive a decision, and if approved, complete your purchase with the agreed monthly payment schedule instead of a single lump sum.

Financing approval and terms depend on the lender's own credit criteria, and specific rates or promotional terms are provided directly by the lender during the application process.

sections.heading: How to apply
sections.body: Once you have a finalized quote for your cabinet order, let us know you would like to explore financing and we will point you to the lender's application. You will typically get a decision quickly, and if approved you can confirm your cabinet order using the financing plan instead of e-transfer or a card invoice.

sections.heading: Our Lowest Price Guarantee
sections.body:
If you find the same White Shaker RTA cabinet advertised for less by another Canadian retailer, we will match that price. To request a match, the comparison must meet a few reasonable conditions:
- The product must be identical, same style, colour, and dimensions
- The competitor must have the item in stock and available for purchase
- The price must be verifiable, such as a link to the live listing or a dated screenshot
- The request must be made before you complete your purchase with us

Send the details to service@rtacabinetscanada.ca along with your quote and we will review the comparison and confirm your matched price.

sections.heading: Why we can offer this
sections.body: Because we sell RTA cabinets directly and ship efficiently as flat packed freight, we are able to keep pricing competitive without cutting corners on materials. The Lowest Price Guarantee exists so you can compare confidently, knowing that if a genuinely identical product is available for less elsewhere, we will meet that price rather than lose your business over it.

sections.heading: Combining financing with a price match
sections.body: Financing and the Lowest Price Guarantee can be used together. If you have a verified lower price from another retailer, submit it before your purchase is finalized so we can apply the matched price to your quote, and then choose whether to pay by e-transfer, card invoice, or financing based on that final, matched total.

sections.heading: Planning your budget
sections.body: Whether you plan to pay upfront or use financing, it helps to build your full cabinet list in the free 3D Kitchen Planner at /planner before requesting a quote, so the number you are financing or comparing against a competitor reflects your complete kitchen rather than a partial estimate. If your plans change after your initial quote, such as adding an island or extra wall cabinets, let us know and we will update your quote before you confirm your order or finalize a financing application.

sections.heading: Other ways to manage cost
sections.body: Beyond financing and the Lowest Price Guarantee, a few practical choices can help manage your total project cost. Assembling cabinets yourself instead of using our expert assembly service saves the 75 dollar per cabinet fee, while delivery is free for any address within 300 km of London, Ontario. Phasing a renovation, such as ordering base cabinets first and wall cabinets in a second order, is also an option worth discussing with us if you want to spread cost over a longer timeline outside of formal financing.

faqs.q: Is there a credit check for financing?
faqs.a: Financing is subject to approval through our third party lender's own application and credit review process. You will receive a decision after applying.

faqs.q: What counts as an identical product for the price match?
faqs.a: The item must be the exact same cabinet style, colour, and dimensions, currently in stock at the competitor, and the price must be verifiable through a live link or dated screenshot.

faqs.q: Can I request a price match after I have already ordered?
faqs.a: Price match requests need to be made before your purchase is completed with us. If you have a comparison in hand, reach out before confirming your order so we can review it.

title: Caring for Your Painted White Shaker Cabinets
description: Simple daily cleaning, stain prevention, and long term care tips to keep your painted White Shaker RTA cabinets looking new for years.
intro: Painted white cabinets are durable and easy to live with when cared for properly. A little routine attention goes a long way toward keeping your White Shaker kitchen looking fresh for years to come.

sections.heading: Daily cleaning
sections.body: Wipe down cabinet surfaces regularly with a soft, damp microfiber cloth to remove dust, fingerprints, and light kitchen grime. For most day to day cleaning, water alone is enough. If you need extra cleaning power, use a small amount of mild dish soap diluted in warm water, applied with a soft cloth rather than sprayed directly onto the cabinet.

sections.heading: What to avoid
sections.body:
- Abrasive sponges, scouring pads, or powdered cleansers, which can dull or scratch the painted finish
- Harsh chemical cleaners, bleach, or ammonia based products
- Excess standing water, especially around the sink cabinet and any areas near appliances that generate steam
- Wiping with dry paper towel on stubborn spots, which can create fine scratches over time, use a damp cloth instead

sections.heading: Preventing stains and heat damage
sections.body: Wipe up spills, especially oil, wine, and acidic foods like tomato sauce or citrus, as soon as possible rather than letting them sit on the finish. Use trivets or heat pads for hot pots and pans near cabinet surfaces, and avoid placing small appliances that generate heat, such as toaster ovens, directly against cabinet doors or the underside of wall cabinets.

sections.heading: Caring for hardware and hinges
sections.body: Soft close hinges and drawer glides are self contained and do not require regular maintenance, but keeping tracks free of dust and debris helps them operate smoothly over time. If a door or drawer starts to feel less smooth, a light wipe down of the glide track with a dry cloth is usually enough. Hardware such as pulls and knobs can be cleaned with the same mild soap and water approach as the cabinet surfaces.

sections.heading: Handling minor scuffs
sections.body: Light scuffs can often be gently buffed out with a soft cloth and a small amount of mild soap and water. For anything beyond light surface marks, avoid do it yourself touch up paint unless it is specifically matched, since mismatched paint is more noticeable than a minor mark. If you have concerns about a specific mark, contact us at service@rtacabinetscanada.ca and we can advise on the best approach.

sections.heading: Long term care
sections.body: Maintain reasonable humidity levels in your kitchen where possible, since extreme swings in humidity can affect painted wood surfaces over time. Periodically check that door and drawer hardware is still tight, since normal daily use can loosen screws slightly over months and years, and a quick tightening keeps everything operating smoothly.

sections.heading: Protecting cabinets around the sink and dishwasher
sections.body: The sink cabinet and any cabinets next to a dishwasher see more moisture exposure than the rest of the kitchen. Wipe up splashes around the sink promptly, and check occasionally under the sink for any slow leaks from supply lines or the drain trap, since standing water against a cabinet floor is one of the more common sources of long term damage in any kitchen. If your dishwasher door releases steam when opened, give the adjacent cabinet door a quick wipe afterward rather than letting condensation sit on the painted surface.

sections.heading: Seasonal care checklist
sections.body:
A simple seasonal routine keeps your kitchen looking its best with minimal effort:
- Wipe down all cabinet surfaces with a damp cloth and check for any missed spots near the stove and sink
- Tighten any loose hinge screws or drawer glide screws
- Check that soft close doors and drawers are still closing smoothly, and adjust hinges slightly if a door has started to sag
- Dust the tops of wall cabinets if your kitchen does not have crown moulding sealing that gap

A few minutes each season is usually all it takes to keep a painted White Shaker kitchen looking as good as the day it was installed.

faqs.q: Can I use regular kitchen cleaning spray on my cabinets?
faqs.a: We recommend sticking to a soft damp cloth with water or a small amount of mild dish soap. Many all purpose sprays contain ingredients that can dull a painted finish over time.

faqs.q: How do I remove grease buildup near the stove?
faqs.a: Use a soft cloth with warm water and a small amount of mild dish soap, working in gentle circles. Avoid abrasive pads, which can scratch the painted surface even when the grease itself comes off easily.

faqs.q: Will my white cabinets yellow over time?
faqs.a: Quality painted finishes are formulated to resist yellowing under normal kitchen conditions. Keeping cabinets clean and out of prolonged direct sun exposure where possible helps preserve the finish over the long run.
